verdict.rationale: Fern's changelog refers to a self-hosted container that serves documentation pages and resolves environment variables per request, which implies a first-party self-hosted docs deployment. The only evidence is a changelog line: there are no setup docs, no stated plan or licensing requirements, and no confirmation that the full platform runs self-hosted. The community note that Fern is 'open-source, though not free' is about licensing and does not establish self-hosting. missing for 10: dedicated self-hosting deployment documentation, clarity on which components (docs, Ask Fern, editor) can be self-hosted, plan/licensing requirements, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: A self-hosted container can now resolve environment variables in the pages it serves, on each request... so one image serves deployments that differ only in those values.
